children: Aurora Cannabis is urging its shareholders to reject an unsolicited $272 million hostile takeover bid from Curaleaf Holdings, calling the offer inadequate and an attempt to use Aurora's clean balance sheet to absorb Curaleaf's heavy debt load.

The Aurora board's unanimous recommendation to take no action escalates the defensive stance it has taken since Curaleaf made its offer earlier last month. Aurora said the capped bid offers no meaningful change-of-control premium for its high-margin European operations and that it would subject investors to a share structure that would leave them with a 3.2% vote despite an equity stake of 7.7%.

Furthermore, Aurora said the transaction effectively uses its liquid assets to bail out Curaleaf's leveraged balance sheet, noting Aurora is debt-free and holds $149 million in cash and liquid assets, compared with Curaleaf's total debt and financial obligations of more than $1 billion.

The formal rejection follows Curaleaf going directly to Aurora shareholders after private talks had stalled between the two companies. Curaleaf's offer of $4 a share is made up of 0.3463 of a Curaleaf subordinate voting share and 75 cents in cash. The deal is subject to a maximum cap of $5 a share, Curaleaf said last month.

Aurora's board on Wednesday reiterated its confidence in its standalone plan, citing record international revenue and high margins. It also cited recent expansion of its EU-GMP cultivation and manufacturing capacity, or that which has passed European Union good-manufacturing-practice guidelines.
Curaleaf's formal tender is open for acceptance until Dec. 1.
